sections.heading: Furnace and AC Repair in Wichita: Find the Cause, Then Fix It
body: Most no-heat and no-cooling calls come down to one part. Too many companies quote the whole system before they've found it. Here's what we look for, and what it usually takes.

items.title: The furnace clicks but never lights
items.text: Usually a worn igniter or a dirty flame sensor. Both are small parts, and it's a short repair once we've confirmed which one.

items.title: It lights, then shuts off after a few minutes
items.text: Often a clogged filter making the furnace overheat, or a sensor that can't prove the flame. We check airflow first, because a new part won't fix a choked filter.

items.title: The AC hums but won't start
items.text: A weak capacitor is the most common cause. It's one of the smallest and cheapest repairs in the trade.

items.title: The house won't cool below 80
items.text: A refrigerant leak or a frozen coil. Adding refrigerant without finding the leak is money that leaks out again, so we find the leak first.

items.title: A motor that squeals, rattles or runs hot
items.text: Blower and condenser motors warn you before they fail. Replacing one early is a smaller job than replacing it after it quits.

items.title: A cracked heat exchanger
items.text: This one isn't small. It keeps burner exhaust out of the air you breathe. If we find a crack, you'll hear it straight, with your options.

sections.heading: What Usually Goes Wrong
body: The house won't cool below 80, the vent air is lukewarm, the outdoor fan isn't spinning, or the breaker trips every time it starts. Most of the time it's one of a short list of parts.
Ice on the copper line, water around the indoor unit and a system that cycles on and off every few minutes mean turn it off and call. Running a struggling air conditioner makes a small repair bigger.

items.title: Capacitor
items.text: Gives the compressor and fan motor the jolt they need to start. When it weakens, the unit hums and won't run. It's one of the most common and cheapest repairs.

items.title: Dirty coil or clogged filter
items.text: Dust and a choked filter cut airflow until the coil freezes into a block of ice. The fix is cleaning, and finding out why it got that way.

items.title: Low refrigerant
items.text: An air conditioner doesn't use it up, so low means a leak. Adding more without fixing the leak is money that drains away again.

items.title: Fan or compressor motor
items.text: A noisy or slow-spinning motor is a warning. Replacing it early is a far smaller job than waiting for it to fail.

sections.heading: What Usually Stops the Heat
body: The thermostat calls for heat and nothing happens, you hear clicking but the burners never light, or the furnace runs a couple of minutes and shuts off, over and over. Cold rooms, a screaming blower and air that isn't warm are worth a call too.
A furnace goes through several steps before it heats your house, and a failure at any one stops the whole thing. That's why most no-heat calls turn out to be a small part and not a new furnace.

items.title: Igniter
items.text: Lights the burner and wears out with use. A cracked or weak igniter means the furnace tries to start and can't.

items.title: Flame sensor
items.text: This small rod tells the furnace the burner lit. When residue coats it, the furnace shuts down after a few seconds as a safety measure. Cleaning or replacing it is a simple repair.

items.title: Filter and airflow
items.text: A clogged filter makes the furnace overheat and shut itself off. It's the cheapest fix there is, and the reason some furnaces cycle on and off.

items.title: Blower motor
items.text: Moves the warm air through the house. When it fails, the furnace can run and you still get little or no warmth in the rooms.

sections.heading: Repair or New Furnace?
body: Here's a rule you can check. If it's an igniter, a sensor or a motor, repair is the answer. It costs far less than a furnace, and the furnace goes on heating your house.
If the furnace is old, the repairs keep coming, or the heat exchanger has failed, that's when to price a new one. Spending a lot on an old furnace is often money better put toward a new one.

The heat exchanger is the metal chamber that keeps burner exhaust apart from the air you breathe. A crack in it is a safety problem, not an inconvenience. If we find one, you'll hear it straight, with what it means and what your options are. A working carbon monoxide detector on every floor is worth having either way.
We put the repair next to a new furnace and tell you which side of the line you're on. If it's time to replace, we install new furnaces and heating systems too.

sections.heading: Keeping a Furnace Healthy
body: Furnaces fail hardest in the first cold snap, after sitting idle all summer. Dust builds up, parts stiffen and a weak igniter finally gives out.
A check before heating season catches those things while it's still warm outside. We offer maintenance plans, so ask about one when you call. Changing the filter on a schedule helps too.

sections.heading: Before You Call
body: If you can do it safely, check a few things first. Make sure the thermostat is set to heat and the batteries are fresh. Check that the furnace switch is on, and that the filter isn't packed with dust.
If you smell gas, leave the house and call your gas company before anything else. Otherwise, if the furnace still won't run, call us.

footer.about: Integrity Heating and Cooling is a family-owned HVAC company in Wichita. Sam and the team repair and replace heating and cooling systems for homes and commercial buildings.
why: We clean up after the job

Your heating and AC pages promise “24/7 Emergency Repair Service.” Your contact page says Monday to Friday, 8 to 5, weekends “at additional cost.” Someone with no heat on a Saturday gets two answers, and that is the call you most need to win.

Your customers already describe the weekend calls you answer. Dayna B.: “Our AC went out called and Sam here in hour on a Saturday morning.” Madison S.: “They offer competitive pricing and shoot you straight.” Today those words sit on Google, not on your site.
So the demo tells one story everywhere: your hours, and what to do when the system quits outside them. It opens with HVAC company in Wichita, KS, and gives AC repair and furnace repair a page each.
